About Lyra Health
Lyra Health is a leading provider of evidence-based mental health care, serving more than 20 million people globally in partnership with employers and more than 100 million through health plan and partner relationships. The company has delivered more than 15 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 35 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness, and cost efficiency. Extensive peer-reviewed research confirms Lyra’s transformative care model helps people recover twice as fast and results in a 26% annual reduction in overall healthcare claims costs. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions. 


About the Role: 
Lyra is seeking an enthusiastic, highly organized, and seasoned Executive Assistant to support our new Chief People Officer (CPO) while overseeing operations for our Santa Monica office space. In this dual-impact role, you will serve as a strategic partner and extension of the CPO, managing seamless day-to-day operations, executive communications, and high-priority People team initiatives. Additionally, you will serve as the heartbeat of our Santa Monica office, a strong ambassador of our company and local culture, office management, and spatial and event logistics.
Your warm, approachable style, high emotional intelligence, and commitment to discretion and confidentiality will be integral to supporting our executive leadership and cultivating an engaging workplace culture.

Additionally, you will serve as the heartbeat of our Santa Monica office, a strong ambassador of our company and local culture, office management, and spatial and event logistics.

lists.content:
Executive Support (Chief People Officer)

  • Manage complex calendar scheduling, travel logistics, and day-to-day priorities for the Chief People Officer.

  • Handle sensitive, confidential HR, personnel, and organizational planning data with complete discretion.

  • Screen, prioritize, and manage incoming executive correspondence, ensuring timely follow-ups and seamless communication flow.

  • Draft, edit, and proof executive communications, presentation decks, and strategic materials for internal leadership and external partners.

  • Provide support for Board of Directors and Compensation Committee meetings, including compiling materials, taking meeting minutes, and tracking action items.

  • Facilitate communication and alignment between the CPO, the People/Talent teams, and key internal/external business stakeholders.

    •  

    Santa Monica Office Management

  • Oversee day-to-day operations of the Santa Monica office space, ensuring a functional, clean, welcoming, and productive work environment.

  • Act as the primary on-site point of contact for Santa Monica employees, visiting executives, property management, vendors, and guests.

  • Manage office vendor relationships, facilities logistics, physical access/security badges, office supplies, catering, and mail/deliveries.

  • Plan and execute local Santa Monica culture initiatives, team-building activities, holiday events, and hybrid/onsite meeting logistics.

  • Maintain office budget tracking, expense reporting, and vendor invoicing.

• 8+ years of experience supporting C-Suite executives; direct experience supporting a CPO, CHRO, or CEO preferred.

  • Proven experience managing physical office space operations and facilities logistics.

  • Background in a fast-paced, growth-stage, or public company environment.

  • Deep experience handling sensitive and confidential HR/personnel information with absolute discretion.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with high attention to detail.

  • Kind, warm, positive, and proactive demeanor with a strong customer-service mindset.

  • High adaptability to changing priorities in a dynamic, hybrid work setup.

  • Advanced proficiency with Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Slides), Slack, and modern workplace tools.

  • Ability to be on-site at the Santa Monica office on a hybrid/regular schedule as required by office operations and CPO presence.

salaryDescription:
As a full-time Executive Assistant, you will be employed by Lyra Health, Inc. The anticipated annual base salary range for this full-time position is $118,000 to $162,500. The base range is determined by role and level, and placement within the range will depend on a number of job-related factors, including but not limited to your skills, qualifications, experience and location. This role may also be eligible for discretionary bonuses.  

Annual salary is only one part of an employee’s total compensation package at Lyra. We also offer generous benefits that include: 

  • Comprehensive healthcare coverage (including medical, dental, vision, FSA/HSA, life and disability insurances)

  • Lyra for Lyrians; coaching and therapy services

  • Equity in the company through discretionary restricted stock units

  • Competitive time off with pay policies including vacation, sick days, and company holidays

  • Paid parental leave 

  • 401K with up to 3% matching

  • Monthly tech allowance

  • We like to spread joy throughout the year with well-being perks and activities, surprise swag, regular community celebration…and more!  

We can’t wait to meet you.

About The Role
Lyra Health’s Clinical Strategy team is seeking a seasoned Senior Operations Lead for a high-impact, 6-month contract engagement focused on driving our Joint Commission (TJC) Behavioral Health Care and Human Services (BHC) accreditation readiness.
This role sits at the intersection of clinical strategy, regulatory execution, and cross-functional project management. Acting as the primary project lead, you will bridge the gap between Clinical Strategy, Clinical Operations, and key cross-functional teams to drive our accreditation roadmap.

About The Role

Lyra Health’s Clinical Strategy team is seeking a seasoned Senior Operations Lead for a high-impact, 6-month contract engagement focused on driving our Joint Commission (TJC) Behavioral Health Care and Human Services (BHC) accreditation readiness.

This role sits at the intersection of clinical strategy, regulatory execution, and cross-functional project management. Acting as the primary project lead, you will bridge the gap between Clinical Strategy, Clinical Operations, and key cross-functional teams to drive our accreditation roadmap.

This role is ideal for a senior healthcare project manager who excels at translating complex regulatory mandates or compliance standards into actionable project plans. While familiarity with Joint Commission standards is preferred, we are primarily seeking an exceptional operational lead who can quickly get up to speed on TJC requirements, partner with clinical domain experts, and drive execution. You are a self-directed player-coach who is comfortable getting "in the weeds" with workstream leads to build compliance documentation while also zooming out to present a 30,000-foot risk assessment to leadership.

lists.content:
As a senior contractor, you will hit the ground running and lead the execution of our TJC survey readiness roadmap:

  • Roadmap & Work Plan Ownership: Refine, maintain, and drive the master Project Work Plan for TJC Behavioral Health and Telehealth accreditation readiness, establishing clear workstream milestones across clinical and operational teams.

  • Gap Analysis & Risk Mitigation: Continuously identify gaps, compliance risks, and cross-functional dependencies; proactively update the roadmap and implement risk mitigation strategies.

  • Workstream Facilitation: Partner directly with workstream leads to deep-dive into specific TJC standards. Develop supporting materials and process documentation as needed.

  • Mock Survey & Readiness Execution: Organize and project manage internal mock audits, tracer activities, and readiness drills to ensure operational teams are fully prepared for survey execution.

  • Governance & Cross-Functional Alignment: Establish clear communication cadences across stakeholders (live working groups, asynchronous updates, and project dashboards) to drive cross-functional accountability.

  • Executive Visibility: Develop concise, data-driven written updates for senior leadership to highlight progress, key milestones, and critical risks.

• 10+ years of healthcare project management, healthcare operations, or management consulting experience, preferably within high-growth health tech or clinical environments

  • Demonstrated track record of leading complex, cross-functional regulatory, compliance, or accreditation readiness initiatives from gap analysis through execution

  • Exceptional strategic and project management skills with the ability to influence cross-functional peers and senior leadership without direct authority

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; proven ability to distill complex clinical insights and regulatory requirements into actionable executive summaries

  • A highly organized self-starter who thrives in fast-paced, dynamic environments and can create structure out of ambiguity

  • Deep passion for expanding access to high-quality, evidence-based mental health care

• Direct experience or familiarity with the accreditation process (e.g., The Joint Commission, CARF, NCQA, or other), specifically within Behavioral Health Care and Human Services (BHC) or virtual/telehealth models

The company has delivered more than 15 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 35 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness, and cost efficiency. Lyra members have access to care in one day, and nine out of ten improve with the support of providers like you. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions. You will be contracted by Lyra Clinical Associates.


About the Opportunity
 
*For this opportunity, we are looking for a Licensed Therapist that provides care to children and/or adolescents. We are also looking for a provider that can provide in–person care.
 
Lyra’s provider network is composed of in-person and virtual therapists, physicians, and coaches across the US. With our advanced matching technology, supportive provider platform, and opportunities for training and clinical consultation, being part of our network is an incredible chance to do what you love (like client care) with support for the things you don’t love (like self promotion and scheduling).
 
This opportunity is a great fit if you’re an independently licensed clinical therapist interested in providing culturally responsive, evidence-based therapy for children, adults, couples, and/or families. We encourage clinicians to apply who have experience with caseloads that include a comprehensive spectrum of mental health needs, from milder presentations to more complex and severe support. This opportunity is a great fit for providers seeking well-matched and motivated clients, administrative and marketing support, and easy invoicing with quick payments. The ability to work with clients in person through your private or group practice is strongly preferred. We are looking for clinicians who are able to work with clients in these locations: Charlotte, NC

Lyra members have access to care in one day, and nine out of ten improve with the support of providers like you. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions. You will be contracted by Lyra Clinical Associates.

descriptionBody:
About the Opportunity
 
*For this opportunity, we are looking for a Licensed Therapist that provides care to children and/or adolescents. We are also looking for a provider that can provide in–person care.
 
Lyra’s provider network is composed of in-person and virtual therapists, physicians, and coaches across the US. With our advanced matching technology, supportive provider platform, and opportunities for training and clinical consultation, being part of our network is an incredible chance to do what you love (like client care) with support for the things you don’t love (like self promotion and scheduling).
 
This opportunity is a great fit if you’re an independently licensed clinical therapist interested in providing culturally responsive, evidence-based therapy for children, adults, couples, and/or families. We encourage clinicians to apply who have experience with caseloads that include a comprehensive spectrum of mental health needs, from milder presentations to more complex and severe support. This opportunity is a great fit for providers seeking well-matched and motivated clients, administrative and marketing support, and easy invoicing with quick payments. The ability to work with clients in person through your private or group practice is strongly preferred. We are looking for clinicians who are able to work with clients in these locations: Charlotte, NC
